skill.name: markdown-url
skill.description: Convert HTTP and HTTPS destinations into markdown.new URLs for cleaner reading and text extraction.
skill.summary: Create markdown.new proxy links for readable web content.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Most external-command and filesystem detections are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and a URL-scheme regex. The skill intentionally routes suitable URLs through markdown.new, creating a third-party network dependency that may expose destination URLs. No prompt injection or command execution behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Destination URLs are disclosed to a third-party proxy.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before proxying and reject URLs containing credentials, sensitive query parameters, private hosts, or confidential resource identifiers.

content.user_title: Convert Web Pages into Clean Markdown
content.value_statement: Web pages can be difficult to extract and summarize. This skill routes suitable public pages through markdown.new for cleaner Markdown content.
actual_capabilities: Normalizes bare hosts and paths into HTTPS URLs.
Preserves existing HTTP and HTTPS destinations.
Prefixes destinations with the markdown.new service URL.
Defines fallback rules for blocked or incomplete proxy responses.
Provides a Node command-line helper that prints transformed URLs.
limitations: The workflow depends on the availability and behavior of markdown.new.
Authenticated, private, interactive, and payment pages should use the original site.
JavaScript applications, paywalls, CAPTCHAs, and bot controls may prevent extraction.
The command-line helper only rewrites URLs; it does not fetch or validate page content.

use_cases.title: Read technical documentation
use_cases.description: Convert public documentation links into cleaner Markdown before summarizing or taking notes.

use_cases.title: Prepare research notes
use_cases.description: Open public articles through a text-focused view for easier quotation and structured note creation.

use_cases.title: Review publication content
use_cases.description: Transform public blog posts and changelogs into readable Markdown for editing and comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Convert one URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [public URL] into a markdown.new URL. Return only the transformed destination.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a simple public page.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [documentation URL] through markdown.new, then summarize the main concepts and list important configuration details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for public technical documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Extract structured notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Read [article URL] through markdown.new. Produce headings, key claims, supporting details, and source quotations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when preparing research notes.

prompt_templates.title: Apply fallback policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Try [public URL] through markdown.new once. If blocked or incomplete, use the original page and clearly identify the fallback.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when proxy compatibility is uncertain.

output_examples.input: Prepare notes from a public product changelog.
output_examples.output: A structured summary with release headings, major changes, compatibility notes, and concise source quotations.

output_examples.input: The proxy returns an access-denied response.
output_examples.output: The markdown.new view was blocked, so the original public page was used for the summary.

best_practices: Use the proxy only for public, read-only pages.
Inspect URLs for credentials or sensitive query parameters before rewriting them.
Fall back to the original page after one failed proxy attempt.
anti_patterns: Do not route login, OAuth, payment, upload, or authenticated workflows through the proxy.
Do not rewrite local paths or non-HTTP schemes.
Do not repeatedly retry blocked pages or bypass access controls.

faq.question: Does this skill download web pages?
faq.answer: The helper only prints a rewritten URL. An agent may visit that URL when performing the documented workflow.

faq.question: Which URL schemes are supported?
faq.answer: The helper accepts HTTP and HTTPS destinations. Bare hosts are normalized to HTTPS.

faq.question: Can it process authenticated pages?
faq.answer: No. Use the original site for pages requiring cookies, sessions, login, OAuth, or private access.

faq.question: What happens when markdown.new fails?
faq.answer: The workflow switches to the original page after one failed or incomplete proxy attempt.

faq.question: Does it preserve query parameters?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper preserves the supplied HTTP or HTTPS URL when adding the service prefix.

faq.question: Is every public URL suitable?
faq.answer: No. Interactive applications, paywalls, CAPTCHAs, and access-controlled pages may not work correctly.
